title: Responsive Grid component for React and Next.js
description: Compose typed CSS Grid layouts with responsive columns, auto-fit and auto-fill sizing, item spans, named areas, and themeable surfaces.

intro: Build dashboards, forms, and card collections with a CSS-driven Grid. Configure responsive layouts and item placement without measuring the viewport in JavaScript. Keep arbitrary React content and native controls inside neutral or styled items.
useCases: Card collections that fit their available container width.
Forms and account sections with named areas.
Nested layouts with shared spacing and appearance tokens.

faqs.question: What makes Grid dynamic?
faqs.answer: CSS responds to available space and viewport breakpoint variants. Consumers filter, sort, insert, or remove keyed children with normal React state; Grid does not maintain a separate data model.

faqs.question: How does Grid differ from Bento Grid or DataTable?
faqs.answer: Grid provides neutral responsive layout and placement. Bento Grid adds styled feature tiles, expansion, and detail interactions. DataTable provides tabular record behavior such as sorting and selection.

faqs.question: Does Grid require Framer Motion?
faqs.answer: No. The static grid entry has no animation dependency. Reflow animation, drag, resize, and persistence are not part of this initial release.

faqs.question: Are breakpoints based on the viewport or the container?
faqs.answer: Responsive maps use the consumer's Tailwind viewport breakpoints. Auto-fit and auto-fill layouts size columns to the available parent width without breakpoint maps or JavaScript observers.

faqs.question: How do auto-fit and auto-fill differ?
faqs.answer: Auto-fit collapses empty repeated tracks, letting occupied tracks grow. Auto-fill retains empty tracks. Auto layouts support ordinary span-1 items and full-width items; wider numeric spans and explicit column starts normalize to ordinary placement.

faqs.question: How do item spans behave on mobile?
faqs.answer: By default, items stack one per row below the consumer's sm breakpoint, resetting spans, starts, and named areas. Set stackOnMobile={false} to retain the configured mobile layout. From sm upward, the declared layout and placement resume. Consumer style overrides take precedence.

faqs.question: Does CSS Grid require role=grid?
faqs.answer: No. This is a layout component, not an interactive ARIA grid widget. Native list or section semantics and child controls remain available. Explicit placement, dense flow, and named areas can change visual order; keep a meaningful DOM reading sequence.

faqs.question: How do I configure Tailwind scanning?
faqs.answer: Add an @source path to the installed component package relative to your stylesheet. If you vendor Grid through the CLI, include the resulting source folder in Tailwind's scan scope.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.body: Grid supports fixed columns, auto-fit/auto-fill layouts, and custom templates with named areas. GridItem supports responsive spans and starts, optional surfaces, padding, and self-alignment. Native props and refs are retained.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.body: Use Grid as a list with li items or a labeled section when appropriate. Grid does not add focus stops or intercept child keyboard events. Dense flow and explicit placement are opt-in; keep DOM order meaningful for keyboard and screen-reader users.
